meta.title: Best Microwave Under Rs 10,000 in India (2026): Solo, Grill & Convection Picks
meta.description: We ranked 8 microwaves under Rs 10,000 in India -- LG, IFB, Samsung, Bajaj, Morphy Richards. Solo vs grill vs convection, wattage and presets compared.
meta.short_desc: Solo, grill, convection -- which to buy.

headings.text: What actually matters in a microwave under Rs 10,000
Solo vs grill vs convection: which to buy

cta.headline: Right microwave at the right price?
cta.sub: A 20-25L solo or grill microwave from LG, IFB, Samsung, Bajaj or Morphy Richards under Rs 10,000 covers 90 percent of Indian kitchen use. We ranked 8 models on wattage, capacity, presets, build quality, and 1-4 year warranty.

faq.q: What size microwave do I need for an Indian kitchen?
faq.a: 20L for 1-2 person households (reheating, simple cooking). 23-25L for 3-4 person families (most Indian homes -- this is the sweet spot). 28-32L for 5+ person families or if you cook large batches of rice/dal. Below 20L, the turntable is too small for a dinner plate. Above 30L, you pay 30-40 percent more for capacity most Indian kitchens don't need.

faq.q: Solo vs grill vs convection -- which to buy?
faq.a: Solo: reheating, defrosting, simple cooking (dal, rice, basic curries). Rs 5,000-8,000. Grill: solo + grilling (paneer tikka, kebabs, bread pizza). Rs 7,000-12,000. Convection: solo + grill + baking (cakes, pizzas, tandoori). Rs 9,000-18,000. For most Indian kitchens, grill (Rs 7,000-10,000) is the right pick -- convection is only worth it if you bake at least twice a month.

faq.q: How much electricity does a microwave use?
faq.a: A 20-25L solo microwave uses 800-900W on high (about 0.8-0.9 units per hour of cooking). Reheating 3-4 rotis + dal + sabzi for a family of 4 uses about 0.3-0.4 units (Rs 2-3). Grill and convection modes use 50-100 percent more electricity because they heat the heating element + magnetron. Inverter microwaves (LG, Panasonic, Samsung premium) cut this by 20-30 percent.

faq.q: What is a microwave inverter and is it worth the price?
faq.a: Inverter technology varies the magnetron power continuously instead of cycling on/off at full power. The result: more even cooking (no cold spots in dal), faster reheating (15-20 percent less time), and 20-30 percent less electricity. Inverter microwaves cost Rs 1,500-3,000 more than non-inverter equivalents and are worth it if you cook daily. Inverter is rare under Rs 10,000 -- most picks below are non-inverter.

faq.q: Is a convection microwave under Rs 10,000 worth buying?
faq.a: Marginal. The convection microwave ovens under Rs 10,000 (e.g. IFB 20SC2, Morphy Richards 25CG) cut corners on heating element quality and fan speed. They bake unevenly and the convection fan makes more noise than Rs 15,000+ models. If you bake weekly, stretch to Rs 12,000-15,000 for an LG MC2886BRUM or IFB 30BRC2. If you only want convection for occasional pizza and cake, a Rs 9,000 convection is fine.

meta.tldr_pick: Our top pick is the LG MS2043DB (20L Solo Microwave). 700W output, 20L capacity (ideal for 2-3 person families), i-Wave technology for even cooking, anti-bacterial cavity, 1-year warranty on product + 4 years on magnetron. Rs 6,490 on Amazon during sale weeks. The most reliable solo microwave in India.
key_takeaways: 20-25L is the sweet spot for Indian kitchens; below 20L cannot fit a dinner plate.
Solo (Rs 5-8k) for reheating only. Grill (Rs 7-10k) is the best balance for Indian cooking.
700-900W output is the floor -- below 700W, reheating takes 50 percent longer.
Magnetron warranty (3-4 years) matters more than product warranty (1 year).
meta.who_for: Indian families and bachelors looking for a reliable microwave under Rs 10,000 for reheating, defrosting, simple Indian cooking (dal, rice, curry) and basic grilling. Ideal for 2-4 person households, kitchen renters, and PG/shared-room setups where an OTG is not feasible.
meta.methodology: We compared 8 microwaves under Rs 10,000 from LG, IFB, Samsung, Bajaj, Morphy Richards, Panasonic and Godrej. For each, we evaluated capacity, output wattage, mode (solo/grill/convection), i-Wave or inverter technology, presets relevant to Indian cooking, child lock, build quality of the cavity (anti-bacterial coating), warranty on magnetron vs body, and brand service network. Cross-referenced with 2026 buyer reviews. Reviewed every 30 days.

body:
What actually matters in a microwave under Rs 10,000

Three numbers decide whether a microwave under Rs 10,000 actually works in an Indian kitchen: capacity, output wattage, and mode (solo/grill/convection). Everything else -- presets, child lock, display color -- is decoration.

The under-Rs 10,000 microwave market in India is dominated by LG, IFB, Samsung, Bajaj, Morphy Richards and Panasonic. There are 200+ models in this segment on Amazon India alone, and most of them are differentiated by feature lists rather than cooking performance. After ranking 8 of the strongest models, the choice comes down to how you actually use the microwave: reheating only, daily Indian cooking, or occasional baking.

For most Indian kitchens, a 20-25L microwave with 700-900W output and grill mode under Rs 10,000 is the right pick. The 4 picks below match this shape.

  • Capacity -- 20L for 1-2 person households. 23-25L for 3-4 person families (most Indian homes). Below 20L, the turntable is too small for a dinner plate. Above 30L, you pay 30-40 percent more for capacity you do not need.
  • Output wattage -- 700W minimum (LG MS2043DB sits at this floor). 800-900W is the sweet spot for fast reheating. Below 700W, reheating takes 50 percent longer -- frustrating when you are heating lunch in 90 seconds versus 3 minutes.
  • Mode (solo vs grill vs convection) -- Solo for reheating, defrosting, simple cooking. Grill adds grilling (paneer tikka, kebabs). Convection adds baking (cakes, pizzas, tandoori). For most Indian kitchens, grill is the right pick -- convection is only worth it if you bake weekly.
  • Magnetron warranty -- The magnetron is the heart of the microwave. 3-4 year magnetron warranty (LG, Panasonic) signals confidence in long-term reliability. 1-year product warranty + 1-year magnetron is the floor.
If you only buy one thing from this list: the LG MS2043DB Solo Microwave. 700W output, 20L capacity, i-Wave technology (no cold spots in dal), anti-bacterial cavity, and a 4-year magnetron warranty. Rs 6,490 is not the cheapest 20L solo, but LG service in 500+ Indian cities and the magnetron warranty make it the lowest total-cost-of-ownership in this segment.

Solo vs grill vs convection: which to buy

Indian microwave buyers often get confused between the three modes because the price difference is small but the use cases are very different.

Solo microwaves (Rs 5,000-8,000) do three things: reheat, defrost, and cook simple dishes (dal, rice, sabzi, idli). The heating is uniform if the microwave has i-Wave or inverter technology. They cannot grill or bake. For bachelors, students, and small families who only reheat and cook basic Indian food, a solo microwave is the right pick.

Grill microwaves (Rs 7,000-12,000) add a heating element that lets you grill paneer tikka, kebabs, bread pizza, and toast sandwiches. They also handle all solo-mode tasks. For Indian kitchens, grill is the sweet spot -- you get solo + grilling without paying for convection features you may not use.

Convection microwaves (Rs 9,000-25,000) add a fan-forced heating element that bakes cakes, pizzas, cookies, and tandoori dishes. The cheap end (under Rs 12,000) has weak convection fans and uneven baking -- the convection mode is mostly a marketing checkbox. The mid-range (Rs 15,000-25,000, like LG MC2886BRUM or IFB 30BRC2) actually bakes well. Stretch to this band if you bake weekly.

For most Indian kitchens, grill mode at Rs 7,000-10,000 is the right pick. Convection under Rs 10,000 is mostly a compromise.

Our top 4 picks under Rs 10,000

Top Pick

1. LG MS2043DB (20L Solo Microwave)

Rs 6,490
Capacity20L
Wattage700W output
ModeSolo
Techi-Wave + anti-bacterial cavity
Warranty1 yr product, 4 yr magnetron

The LG MS2043DB is the most-recommended solo microwave in India for good reason. It pairs a 20L capacity (right for 2-3 person households) with 700W output and LG's i-Wave technology -- a reflector design that distributes microwaves more evenly than the basic stirrer fans in cheaper models.

The result: no cold spots when reheating dal or rice. The anti-bacterial cavity coating (easier to wipe clean) and 4-year magnetron warranty make it the lowest total-cost-of-ownership solo microwave in this segment.

LG service network is the widest in India (500+ cities with on-site repair). If the microwave fails outside warranty, parts are stocked and repairs typically cost Rs 800-1,500.

What works

  • i-Wave technology -- no cold spots in dal or rice
  • 4-year magnetron warranty (longest in this segment)
  • LG service network in 500+ Indian cities
  • Anti-bacterial cavity -- easier to wipe clean
  • Energy-efficient -- 0.6-0.7 units per hour of cooking

Trade-offs

  • Solo only -- cannot grill or bake
  • 700W is the floor (vs 800-900W on competitors)
  • Rs 6,490 is not the cheapest 20L solo
Check price on Amazon
Runner-up

2. IFB 20PG4S (20L Grill Microwave)

Rs 8,290
Capacity20L
Wattage800W output
ModeGrill (solo + grill element)
TechAnti-bacterial cavity
Warranty1 yr product, 1 yr magnetron

The IFB 20PG4S is the best grill microwave under Rs 10,000 for Indian cooking. It pairs a 20L cavity with 800W output and a heating element that lets you grill paneer tikka, kebabs, and bread pizza without preheating an OTG.

IFB's strength in this segment is its Indian-cooking presets -- the 20PG4S has dedicated buttons for dal, rice, curry, idli, and chai. The auto-cook menu is more relevant to Indian kitchens than LG's preset list, which is calibrated for Western dishes.

IFB service is strongest in south India and metros. In north India and tier-2 cities, service response is slower than LG. The 1-year magnetron warranty is shorter than LG's 4 years -- a real consideration for long-term ownership.

What works

  • 800W output -- faster reheating than LG MS2043DB
  • Indian-cooking presets (dal, rice, curry, idli, chai)
  • Grill mode -- paneer tikka, kebabs, bread pizza
  • Anti-bacterial cavity coating

Trade-offs

  • 1-year magnetron warranty vs LG 4 years
  • IFB service network thinner in north India
  • Rs 8,290 is more than Rs 6,490 LG
Check price on Amazon
Best Budget

3. Bajaj 2005ETB (20L Grill Microwave)

Rs 5,990
Capacity20L
Wattage800W output
ModeGrill (solo + grill)
Tech30 auto-cook presets
Warranty1 yr product

The Bajaj 2005ETB is the cheapest grill microwave under Rs 10,000 from an Indian brand. At Rs 5,990, it delivers solo + grill modes with 800W output -- the same spec as the IFB 20PG4S but Rs 2,300 cheaper.

The trade-off: Bajaj's cooking performance is one tier below IFB and LG. The auto-cook presets are not as well-calibrated for Indian dishes (the dal preset overcooks by 30-40 seconds), and the cavity coating wears out faster. The build quality is honest for the price, but the microwave will not last 8-10 years like an LG or IFB.

For budget-first buyers who replace the microwave every 4-5 years anyway, the Bajaj 2005ETB is fine. For long-term owners, spend the extra Rs 2,000-2,500 on the IFB or LG.

What works

  • Rs 5,990 is the cheapest grill microwave under Rs 10,000 from a known brand
  • 800W output matches IFB 20PG4S
  • 30 auto-cook presets (most in this list)
  • Bajaj service centers in 300+ cities

Trade-offs

  • Build quality is mid-tier -- expect 4-5 year lifespan
  • Auto-cook presets less accurate than IFB for Indian dishes
  • Only 1-year warranty (no extended magnetron coverage)
Check price on Amazon

4. Samsung CE73JD-B (21L Convection Microwave)

Rs 9,490
Capacity21L
Wattage800W output
ModeConvection (solo + grill + convection)
TechTandoor technology
Warranty1 yr product

The Samsung CE73JD-B is the cheapest triple-mode microwave (solo + grill + convection) under Rs 10,000 from a top-3 brand. The 21L capacity and 800W output match the IFB 20PG4S, with the addition of convection mode for baking.

Samsung's "Tandoor technology" is a calibrated heating element + fan combination that simulates tandoor cooking at 200-220 degrees C. For naan, tandoori chicken, and pizza, the CE73JD-B does a reasonable job in this price band.

The trade-off: at Rs 9,490, the convection fan is smaller and weaker than Rs 15,000+ Samsung convection models. Baking a cake or pizza works, but it takes longer and the heat distribution is uneven compared to higher-end convection ovens. This is honest convection at a budget price -- not premium convection.

What works

  • Triple-mode: solo + grill + convection
  • 21L capacity -- slightly larger than IFB 20L
  • Samsung Tandoor technology for Indian tandoori-style dishes
  • Rs 9,490 is the cheapest Samsung convection under Rs 10,000

Trade-offs

  • Convection fan is weaker than Rs 15,000+ models
  • Only 1-year warranty
  • Baking takes 10-15 percent longer than premium convection
Check price on Amazon

The one we recommend skipping

The "25L convection for Rs 9,999" trap: brands like Morphy Richards, Lifelong, and several unbranded OEM imports are pushing 25L convection microwaves at Rs 9,999 to compete with LG and IFB. They look attractive on paper -- 25L is bigger than the LG and IFB 20L, convection is included, and the price is the same as the IFB 20PG4S grill-only.

Where they cut corners: (1) magnetron quality is one tier below Japanese or Korean OEMs, (2) convection fan is small and noisy, leading to uneven baking, (3) no anti-bacterial cavity coating (cavity stains and smells persist), (4) 1-year warranty with no extended magnetron coverage. In real Indian kitchens, these budget convection microwaves bake unevenly, last 3-4 years (vs 7-8 years for LG/IFB), and the convection mode is mostly unusable for serious baking.

If your budget is Rs 10,000 and you want convection, stretch Rs 500-1,000 to the Samsung CE73JD-B (Rs 9,490) or wait until you can spend Rs 12,000-15,000 on an LG MC2886BRUM. A 25L convection that does not bake well is wasted money.

Skip

Morphy Richards 25CG (25L Convection, Rs 9,999)

Rs 9,999
Capacity25L
Wattage900W output
ModeConvection (solo + grill + convection)
TechConvection fan weak / noisy
Warranty1 yr

The Morphy Richards 25CG is one of several 25L convection microwaves at Rs 9,999 (also look at Lifelong 25L Convection, BPL 25L Convection, Haier 25L Convection). They have similar specs on paper: 25L, 900W, convection mode, 30+ presets.

In real Indian cooking, the convection fan in these models is the weak link -- it is smaller and slower than the fan in LG MC2886BRUM (Rs 15,490) or IFB 30BRC2 (Rs 16,990). The result: baking a cake takes 10-15 minutes longer and the top is more done than the bottom. The magnetron is also a tier below LG/IFB Japanese/Korean OEM magnetrons, so the unit fails sooner (4-5 years vs 7-8 years).

If you can stretch to Rs 12,000, buy the Samsung CE73JD-B (Rs 9,490) for triple-mode + Samsung reliability, or save Rs 5,000 more for a true convection oven like the LG MC2886BRUM. The Rs 9,999 25L convection is a marketing compromise, not a real deal.

The bottom line

For most Indian kitchens, the LG MS2043DB Solo at Rs 6,490 is the right microwave under Rs 10,000. The 4-year magnetron warranty, i-Wave even-cooking technology, and LG service network make it the lowest total-cost-of-ownership in this segment. For Indian-cooking-specific presets and grill mode, the IFB 20PG4S at Rs 8,290 is the runner-up. For budget-first buyers, the Bajaj 2005ETB at Rs 5,990 is honest value if you accept the 4-5 year lifespan. For triple-mode (convection included) under Rs 10,000, the Samsung CE73JD-B at Rs 9,490 is the right pick.

Skip the 25L Rs 9,999 convection microwaves from Morphy Richards, Lifelong, and BPL -- they look like a deal but bake unevenly and fail within 4-5 years. Save up for an LG MC2886BRUM if you bake weekly.

Decision shortcut: best overall solo -- LG MS2043DB (Rs 6,490). Best grill for Indian cooking -- IFB 20PG4S (Rs 8,290). Best budget -- Bajaj 2005ETB (Rs 5,990). Best triple-mode -- Samsung CE73JD-B (Rs 9,490). Skip -- 25L Rs 9,999 convection microwaves (Morphy Richards 25CG).
